title: Graduate algebra: groups, rings, modules and fields
stage: Graduate study and qualifying exams in mathematics
audience: a graduate student in the first years of a mathematics PhD preparing for qualifying exams, or a graduate preparing to apply for one
purpose: Consolidate and extend algebra to the level of a qualifying exam: group actions and the Sylow theorems, solvable and nilpotent groups, free groups and presentations, rings and localization, modules and exact sequences, modules over a principal ideal domain and canonical forms, tensor products, Noetherian rings and the Hilbert basis theorem, Galois theory and its applications, and an introduction to representations and characters of finite groups.
primary_reading: Course notes by J. S. Milne: Group Theory, and Fields and Galois Theory (free PDF)

weeks.1: Group actions and the Sylow theorems revisited
weeks.2: Solvable and nilpotent groups and composition series
weeks.5: Modules, exact sequences and free modules
weeks.6: Modules over a principal ideal domain
weeks.7: Rational and Jordan canonical forms from module theory
weeks.9: Noetherian rings and the Hilbert basis theorem
weeks.10: Galois theory: separability, normality and the fundamental theorem
weeks.11: Applications of Galois theory: finite fields, cyclotomic extensions and solvability
weeks.12: Representations and characters of finite groups

blocks.deliverable: Classify the groups of a supplied small order.
Find a presentation of a supplied group and verify it.
Decompose a supplied finitely generated abelian group.
Week 7 midterm; derive a canonical form from a module decomposition.
Compute the Galois group of a supplied polynomial.
Build the character table of a small group.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Qualifying-exam dossier in algebra: write complete solutions to twenty exam-style problems across groups, rings, modules and fields, compute the Galois groups of five polynomials with proofs, compute the character tables of S3, D4 and A4 by hand and check their orthogonality relations in plain Python, and write a two-page summary of the structure theorems with their hypotheses.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
